ACT I

SCENE I. A hall by night.

FIRST SPEAKER.
Thou hast the key, and yet thou dost not turn it.
What dost thou fear the open door should show?
The night is old; the fire is fallen low;
And still thou standest as a man of wax.

SECOND SPEAKER.
I have the key, and well I know the lock.
That which I fear lies waiting in the room,
And having seen it once I need not twice.
Thou art too swift to bid me what thou know'st not.

FIRST SPEAKER.
Then give it me, and let me turn it for thee,
For thou hast stood before it all this week.
A fear that is divided is the lighter,
And what thou keepest close will break thy heart.

SECOND SPEAKER.
Thou canst not turn it. It is mine to turn.
The thing within the room was mine to leave,
And mine it is to find again tonight.
Stand by me, then, and hold the lantern high,
And if I falter, do not call me back.

FIRST SPEAKER.
I will not call thee back, nor will I leave thee.
Thy hand is cold; thy face is white as linen.
Speak to me once before thou goest in,
That I may know thy voice if thou come forth changed.

SECOND SPEAKER.
Thou knowest my voice. It will not change for this.
The room holds nothing but what I put there,
A chair, a table, and a letter sealed,
And on the letter is my father's hand.
